headline: Africa: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- Africa: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
- South Asia: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO.
- Western Russia: They got the labs running again after Izium was liberated: Russian strike kills five women who worked at disease control centre.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Vector introduces ready-to-go one-way attack drone.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Vector introduces ready-to-go one-way attack drone.
The company said the Warfighter’s Stack consists of the drone, an HV-ESAD to hold an explosive payload, and a remote control.
- Military Times, 17 hours ago: ‘Inside CENTCOM’ podcast launches amid Iran conflict.
“Inside CENTCOM,” a lifestyle podcast, debuted Thursday against the backdrop of the Iran war.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Lawyers pay it forward - Norman Manley Law School Class of 2001 establishes anniversary fund to support students.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Lawyers pay it forward - Norman Manley Law School Class of 2001 establishes anniversary fund to support students.
The Norman Manley Law School Class of 2001 has committed to establishing a fund to support students at the institution as members marked 25 years since graduating and reflected on the changes that have reshaped the legal profession across the Caribbean. The commitment was announced by Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ) Judge Chantal Ononaiwu, who delivered the keynote remarks at the cohort’s 25th anniversary gala dinner in Kingston on October 31.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: They got the labs running again after Izium was liberated: Russian strike kills five women who worked at disease control centre.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: They got the labs running again after Izium was liberated: Russian strike kills five women who worked at disease control centre.
Five women who worked at a branch of the Kharkiv Oblast Centre for Disease Control and Prevention were killed in a Russian guided aerial bomb attack on the city of Izium on 29 October. They had been among the first to return to work after Izium was liberated from Russian occupation.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Three injured in Russian aerial bomb attack on Sumy.
Sumy Oblast official has reported three civilian injuries and infrastructure damage following Russian strikes using six guided aerial bombs across four locations.
- The Moscow Times, 6 hours ago: Rare Thundersnow Strikes Ural Mountains, Ripping Off Roofs and Causing Power Outages.
At least one person was reportedly killed in a highway traffic accident in the Sverdlovsk region on Friday morning due to icy road conditions.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 7 hours ago: Russians again strike energy facilities that took three days to repair.
Russian forces attacked several energy facilities belonging to DTEK, the largest private energy company in Ukraine, in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast again on the morning of 6 November, damaging equipment and causing a fire.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Von der Leyen to visit Black Sea amid deadly drone attacks.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Von der Leyen to visit Black Sea amid deadly drone attacks.
The trip comes after at least seven commercial vessels were reportedly struck by drones that many have linked to Russia.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Serbian President’s Controversial Last-Minute Pardons Face Legal Challenges.
Before quitting as head of state, Aleksandar Vucic pardoned various suspects accused of violent attacks on anti-government protesters - decisions that critics say may be illegal and unconstitutional.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Transnistria’s Separatist Leader Decorated by Moscow, Denounced by Moldova.
Moldova has imposed a travel ban on breakaway Transnistria’s leader Vadim Krasnoselsky after Vladimir Putin gave him an award for upholding ‘Russian values’, sparking fresh controversy in the EU candidate state.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Egypt army says hundreds of illegal gold miners arrested.
At least 72 gold miners were killed, last October, by airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border. A rights organisation accused the Egyptian air force of carrying out the attack
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Sudan: Abyei - Deadly Drone Strikes Mark 'New and Concerning' Threat, UN Peacekeeping Chief Warns.
[UN News] Drone strikes that killed at least 30 people in Abyei last month have added "a new and concerning dimension" to security in the disputed area, the UN's peacekeeping chief told the Security Council on Thursday.
- Africanews, 7 hours ago: Russia, Ukraine escalate mutual strikes in Black Sea ahead of Abu Dhabi talks.
Russia’s defense ministry on Thursday claimed its forces struck a cargo ship carrying military supplies in the Black Sea just south of Odesa. This follows months of continuous attacks by Ukraine on vessels entering and leaving Russian ports in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 14 hours ago: Africa: Children At Risk As War Zone Attacks On Water and Sanitation More Than Triple.
[UN News] Attacks that damaged or destroyed water and sanitation systems in conflict zones tripled between 2021 and 2025, increasing children's risk of exposure to disease outbreaks, malnutrition and violence.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: What a Trump-Xi-Putin summit could mean – and what it wouldn’t.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: What a Trump-Xi-Putin summit could mean – and what it wouldn’t.
A Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC would be a coup for Moscow, analysts say, but Beijing appears lukewarm.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 5 hours ago: Russia to UAE, Iran steps up diplomacy amid Trump threats: What we know.

- Jerusalem Post, 9 hours ago: 'You'll know soon enough': Trump leaves door open to devastating new Iran strikes.
"I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office following a meeting with his national security advisers, "but maybe I'll have to."
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: IDF on high alert in Hebron as 20,000 Israelis expected for Shabbat amid terror attack fears.
With 20,000 Israelis expected in Hebron for Shabbat Chayei Sarah, security forces are preparing for possible terror attacks and clashes, with drills simulating simultaneous emergencies.
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Smallholder Farmers Raise Climate Change Concerns, Call for Stronger Policy Action.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 5 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe Smallholder Farmers Raise Climate Change Concerns, Call for Stronger Policy Action.
[263Chat] Smallholder farmers across Zimbabwe have called on policymakers to strengthen climate change mitigation and adaptation measures, warning that changing weather patterns, land degradation and human-wildlife conflicts are increasingly threatening their livelihoods.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 7 hours ago: Namibia: Immanuel Threatens Action Over Labour Reform Delays.
[New Era] Justice minister Fillemon Wise Immanuel has warned members of the Labour Advisory Council and the Employment Equity Commission that they risk removal from their positions if they fail to fulfil their responsibilities.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 7 hours ago: Malawi: 'Ngora Has No Power to Deregister HRDC' - Activist Slams Watchdog As Donor Fears Grow.
[Nyasa Times] A fierce row has erupted after Malawi's NGO regulator moved to deregister the Human Rights Defenders Coalition (HRDC), with veteran activist Redson Munlo insisting the watchdog has no legal authority to strike the influential pressure group off the map.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 7 hours ago: South Africa: Diabetes | Elderly Limpopo Couple Skip Diabetes Medication As Clinic Stockouts Strain Their Pensions.
[Health-e] Elderly couple travels between health facilities searching for chronic diabetes medication. When public facilities run out, they spend more than R1,000 on medicine at private pharmacies. Limpopo Health Department acknowledges medicine supply challenges.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Makkah Defence Alliance secretary general to assume duties in Riyadh soon: FO.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Friday said that the secretary general of the Makkah Defence Alliance, retired Lieutenant General Nauman Mahmood, is expected to assume his responsibilities in Riyadh soon. Mahmood was appointed on Sep 23 as the first secretary general of the alliance between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, signed on Aug 7, empowers the three members to consider an armed attack on one member an attack on all.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Saudi Arabia denies WSJ report claiming Houthis demanded $51bn to halt hostilities.
Saudi Arabia has denied a report by the US-based Wall Street Journal (WSJ) that Yemen’s Houthis had demanded $51 billion from kingdom in return for a “negotiated halt” to the ongoing hostilities between the two sides. A report by the Journal claimed on Thursday that the kingdom had approached the Houthis “to see what it would take to arrive at a negotiated halt to the hostilities”, and the group demanded $51bn in return. The report, citing unnamed sources, further claimed that the Houthis would want to be “officially recognised … as the rulers of Yemen”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Newsroom bomb threats follow escalating European flight hoaxes.
Newsrooms in Ireland and Bulgaria received emailed bomb threats on Friday from a purported “Mikhail Andropov”, claiming responsibility for a widening wave of hoax threats disrupting passenger flights across Europe. The messages, sent to Bulgaria’s Nova TV and the Irish public broadcaster RTE, which evacuated its offices and suspended programming, were headlined “Message to the West” and portrayed the threats as the prelude to a series of attacks on means of transport across Europe. The British broadcaster Sky also said it had received a security threat.
- The Hindu - International, just now: Airstrikes on market in southwestern Yemen kill at least 30, Houthis say.
A Houthi Health Ministry spokesperson, Anees Alsabahi, told Houthi-run TV Al Masirah that 15 people were also wounded in the airstrikes on the market in al-Waziyah in the province of Taiz

- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: A kill switch for epilepsy? China cuts seizures by 92.6% in first human chemogenetic trial.
For people living with refractory epilepsy, the brain is like a city that can suffer a blackout any time lightning strikes. Without warning, an abnormal neural discharge can sweep through the intracranial circuits, leaving behind convulsions, loss of consciousness and years of lingering panic. Shaken by the accuracy ⁠of Iran’s attacks on Bahrain and support for them among some Bahrainis, authorities in the Gulf island ⁠nation have launched a crackdown on Shiite Muslim clerics they accuse of fostering allegiance to Tehran at home. Bahraini officials have framed the move in existential terms, saying Iran seeks to undermine and ultimately topple the leadership of the only Gulf country that is ruled by a Sunni Muslim family but populated mostly by Shiites. Chinese state media showcased several Dongfeng-series missiles on Thursday to mark a key anniversary, including the nuclear-capable DF-61 intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) and the rarely seen DF-100 long-range supersonic cruise missile. The coverage coincided with social media reports suggesting that the PLA Rocket Force might have conducted an inland ICBM test, potentially involving a ground-based mid-course missile interception, although neither activity has been officially...
- South China Morning Post - China, 8 hours ago: Japan deploys AI, specialist teams to counter cyberattack wave.
Japan’s government on Friday compiled a package of emergency measures to address a spate of recent personal data breaches caused by unauthorised access, amid growing public concerns over cybersecurity. Among the measures are promoting the use of artificial intelligence to identify vulnerabilities in computer systems and creating several teams of highly skilled experts. The package was announced at a meeting of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and relevant ministers on Friday. Takaichi instructed...
India - bottom line: Sailor Killed After Missile Attack On Oil Tanker In Persian Gulf.
- NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: Sailor Killed After Missile Attack On Oil Tanker In Persian Gulf.
The Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Velos Sapphire was originally sailing to the Bahrain port of Sitra empty of cargo when the attack happened early on Thursday, Velos Tankers said in a statement.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 6 hours ago: China's helicopter arsenal grows, is India ready for the Himalayan challenge?.
China is significantly enhancing its helicopter capabilities, focusing on new attack and transport models. The People's Liberation Army's investments could shift military balance along the Himalayan frontier against India. India, in response, is strengthening its own helicopter fleet with various indigenous and foreign platforms. Both nations are prioritizing aerial mobility for effective operations in challenging mountainous terrain. The ongoing developments highlight the evolving military dynamics between India and China.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: PM Modi's Sule message; 'tussle' in NCP: Is Maha politics heading for another churn?.
Internal conflicts within the Pawar clan has once again put the party at a crossroads. A meeting of senior NCP leaders with Union home minister Amit Shah amid reports of discontent within the party has fuelled speculations. NCP chief Sunetra Pawar has convened meetings to address unity concerns after Ajit Pawar's death. Rohit Pawar has issued a caution to the family regaridng possible BJP manoeuvres.

Australia - bottom line: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this weekend – and it’s dazzling inside and out.
- The Guardian - Australia, 19 hours ago: Powerhouse Parramatta opens this weekend – and it’s dazzling inside and out.
Coups de théâtre abound in the $915m addition to western Sydney’s skyline, which opens on Saturday with five new exhibitions – and a 23-day festival Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email Dubbed the “Opera House of western Sydney”, Powerhouse Parramatta’s white lattice exoskeleton, composed from 1,300 individual pieces and wrapping 30,000 sq metres of interior space, has already become a familiar landmark. Even better known, perhaps, is the project’s controversial history.

Reducing ‘net overseas migration’ has become a national preoccupation. What does it mean for the people waiting to come in? Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads Each year, tens of thousands of people put their hand up to start a new life in Australia. Now they have found themselves at the centre of the country’s heated debate over migration.
